title: Hook Error Handling
description: Implement robust error handling in custom hooks, covering loading states, retry logic, and graceful degradation.

data.text: Real-world hooks interact with APIs, side effects, and user input that can fail. A well-designed custom hook should expose its error state clearly, provide recovery mechanisms, and never crash the entire component tree.
Every async operation in a hook should consider three states: loading, error, and success. Exposing all three gives the consuming component full control over the UI.

data.title: useAsync with Three States
data.content: A reusable hook that manages loading, error, and success states.

data.title: Cancellation Safety
data.text: Always use a cancellation flag inside useEffect to prevent state updates after unmounting. This avoids memory leaks and React warnings about setting state on unmounted components.
Transient failures are common in networked applications. Providing a retry mechanism with exponential backoff prevents overwhelming failing services.

data.title: Hook with Exponential Backoff
data.content: Adding automatic retry logic with increasing delays.

data.text: When a hook fails, the component should still render something useful. Design your hooks to expose fallback data or allow the component to render a degraded UI.

data.title: Degradation Strategies
items: Return cached data alongside the error so the UI does not go blank
Expose an `isFromCache` flag so the component can indicate stale data
Allow the hook to accept a fallback value when all retries fail
Provide an `onError` callback for side effects like logging

data.title: Graceful Degradation Hook
data.content: Returning cached data on failure to keep the UI usable.

data.text: Hooks cannot catch errors in other components, but they can implement internal error boundaries by catching synchronous errors in event handlers and async functions.

data.title: Uncaught Errors Crash Hooks
data.text: An uncaught error inside a hook will propagate up and potentially unmount the component. Always wrap async operations in try-catch blocks and provide meaningful error states.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Expose loading, error, and data states from async hooks
Use cancellation flags to prevent state updates after unmount
Implement retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
Return cached data alongside errors for graceful degradation
data.takeaway: Robust error handling in hooks transforms crashes into recoverable states.
